content.title: About
content.content: Breakfast pizza with egg is a ready‑to‑bake pizza base topped with sauce, cheese, ham and a baked egg in the centre. The dish combines a crispy crust with a soft yolk, providing a hearty and quick breakfast.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Breakfast‑style pizza became popular in the US in the early 2000s as an alternative to traditional eggs.
The egg baked in the middle stays runny if not overcooked, allowing you to “drizzle” it over the other toppings.
The dough is usually made from high‑grade wheat flour, giving the crust a light and airy texture.
Variations may include bacon, spinach, cherry tomatoes or avocado for extra flavor.
The dish can be reheated in a microwave, but an oven gives the best crispy crust.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Egg and ham provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle repair and satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain vitamin B12, while the dough supplies vitamin B1, both important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cheese adds calcium and vitamin D, supporting bone health.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Unlike sweet breakfast options, this pizza contains virtually no sugar, helping to maintain stable blood glucose.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Using reduced‑fat cheese and lean ham keeps the dish moderate in monounsaturated fats.

items.title: Egg or dairy allergy
items.content: People allergic to eggs or dairy should avoid this product.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ham and cheese can be salty; choose low‑sodium versions if you have hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cheese and ham make the pizza relatively calorie‑dense; watch portion size if weight management is a goal.

items.title: Yolk overcooking
items.content: If baked too long, the yolk hardens and loses its characteristic runny texture.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bake the pizza at 180 °C for 8‑10 minutes until the crust is golden and the yolk remains runny. Slice and serve with a green salad or fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen pizza in an airtight bag in the freezer for up to 3 months. After thawing, use within 24 hours and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

coffee-instant-decaffeinated-pre-lighten.title: Instant Coffee, Decaffeinated, Pre‑lightened and Pre‑sweetened with Low‑Calorie Sweetener, Not Reconstituted

content.title: About
content.content: This is an instant, decaffeinated coffee that has already undergone a light roast and is sweetened with a low‑calorie sweetener. The product is ready to use without adding water – it can be dissolved in hot milk or used in cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Instant coffee is made from roasted and ground beans from which caffeine is removed.
Pre‑lightening gives a milder taste without bitterness.
Low‑calorie sweeteners are usually based on stevia or erythritol.
The product is popular in diet nutrition and for people sensitive to caffeine.
Packaging is typically airtight to preserve aroma and freshness.

items.title: Low caffeine content
items.content: The absence of caffeine makes the drink safe for people with insomnia or heightened excitability.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Some studies suggest that instant coffee may help boost metabolic rate.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Despite caffeine removal, the product retains polyphenols that combat free radicals.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: The low‑calorie sweetener allows a sweet taste without extra calories.

items.title: Convenient
items.content: No additional preparation is needed – just add hot liquid.

items.title: Coffee allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to coffee components.

items.title: Sweetener intake
items.content: Excessive consumption of low‑calorie sweeteners can cause gastrointestinal discomfort.

items.title: Flavor loss
items.content: Aroma may diminish over time, so respect the expiration date.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Instant coffee contains fewer minerals than whole beans and should not replace them entirely.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Dissolve a serving in hot water, milk, or a plant‑based beverage. It can be added to smoothies, protein shakes, or used in baking as a sugar substitute.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package. Keep moisture and direct sunlight away. Discard if you notice moldy odor or off‑flavor.

content.title: About
content.content: Catfish fillet is the tender meat of a freshwater fish, obtained after removing bones and skin. When baked or broiled, the fillet has a soft texture, a mildly sweet flavor, and a moderate fat content, making it a popular choice for healthy eating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Catfish belong to the Siluriformes order and are found in rivers and lakes across North America, Europe, and Asia.
The flesh is high in protein and contains few bones, simplifying preparation.
Catfish can breathe air using a specialized organ, allowing them to survive in low‑oxygen waters.
In cuisine, catfish is often prepared "à la française" – baked with herbs and lemon.
Because it is a "soft" fish, catfish is frequently recommended for children and people with digestive sensitivities.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving of catfish fillet provides about 18 g of high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many marine fish, catfish contains relatively little saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Catfish supplies vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals: phosphorus and selenium
items.content: Phosphorus is important for bone health, while selenium acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Moderate omega‑3 content
items.content: Although lower than fatty ocean fish, catfish still contributes omega‑3 fatty acids that benefit cardiovascular health.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Like many freshwater species, catfish can accumulate cadmium and mercury in polluted waters; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content in prepared dishes
items.content: When seasoned with soy sauce or marinades, sodium levels can rise sharply, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Potential parasites
items.content: Raw or undercooked pieces may harbor parasites; always cook to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Catfish fillet can be baked in the oven with lemon, herbs, and olive oil, pan‑seared until golden, or steamed. It is often added to salads, soups, pasta, and rice dishes. Before cooking, rinse and pat dry the fillet, then season with salt and pepper if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh catfish fillet in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic film or an airtight container, for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 3 months. Thaw frozen fillet in the refrigerator before cooking.

infant-formula-gerber-good-start-gentle-.title: Infant formula, Gerber Good Start Gentle, Stage 1, powder, made with baby water

content.title: About
content.content: Gerber Good Start Gentle Stage 1 infant formula is a ready‑to‑use powdered milk designed for newborns and infants from birth to 6 months. The formula features partially hydrolyzed protein, prebiotic GOS, DHA, and specially purified baby water (352) that meets infant water standards.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Good Start Gentle Stage 1 is suitable for babies with increased sensitivity to cow‑milk proteins.
It contains the prebiotic GOS, which supports the growth of beneficial gut bacteria.
The formula is enriched with DHA, an omega‑3 fatty acid important for brain and eye development.
It has undergone clinical testing to confirm safety and efficacy.
Each container holds 400 g of powder, roughly enough for a 30‑day feeding period.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The GOS prebiotic promotes beneficial bacteria, helping regular stools and reducing constipation risk.

items.title: Brain development
items.content: DHA supports neuronal growth and visual function in early life.

items.title: Easy protein absorption
items.content: Partially hydrolyzed protein reduces the digestive load for infants.

items.title: Lower allergy risk
items.content: Hydrolyzed protein and the absence of lactose lower the chance of food‑allergy development.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, E and zinc help strengthen the infant’s immune system.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Despite hydrolysis, some infants may still react to cow‑milk proteins.

items.title: Improper reconstitution
items.content: Over‑concentrated formula can cause dehydration, while overly dilute mixes may lack essential nutrients.

items.title: Storage after opening
items.content: Powder can absorb moisture, leading to clumping and quality loss.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Mix the powder with clean baby water (352) according to the label, typically 1 scoop per 30 ml of water. Stir until smooth and check that the temperature does not exceed 37 °C before feeding.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the container tightly sealed in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Use within 30 days after opening. Discard if the product develops an off‑smell, color change, or unusual taste.

potato-baked-peel-eaten-with-meat.title: Potato, baked, peel eaten, with meat

content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato with the skin left on is a nutritious dish where whole potatoes are roasted, keeping the skin, and then combined with boiled or fried meat (commonly beef, pork or chicken). The skin retains fiber and nutrients, while the meat adds protein and satiety.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato skin contains more vitamin C and fiber than the flesh.
High‑heat baking creates a crisp crust and intensifies flavor.
Baking potatoes in their skins is a tradition in Russia, Germany and the United States.
Meat‑potato combos appear in many national dishes, such as Russian zapekanka or French gratin.
Potatoes are the world’s fourth most produced food after rice, wheat and corn.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide a steady release of energy thanks to slowly digestible starches.

items.title: Source of vitamin C and potassium
items.content: The skin preserves most of the vitamin C, while the tuber is high in potassium, supporting heart function.

items.title: High‑quality protein from meat
items.content: Added meat boosts complete protein content, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Fiber for digestion
items.content: Both the skin and meat fibers help maintain regular bowel movements.

items.title: Low fat when using lean meat
items.content: Choosing lean cuts keeps the dish relatively low in saturated fat.

items.title: Fat and salt content in meat
items.content: Fatty cuts can raise calorie count and saturated fat intake.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to potatoes.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Over‑browning can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen; avoid overly dark crusts.

items.title: Added salt
items.content: Excessively salty meat can increase hypertension risk; monitor salt usage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the baked potato hot, split it open and top with pieces of boiled or fried meat, butter, herbs or spices. The skin is edible and adds a pleasant crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags and reheat in a 180 °C oven to restore the crisp crust.

content.title: About
content.content: Rice, white, with lentils is a ready‑to‑eat product consisting of boiled white rice mixed with cooked lentils. The combination of rice carbohydrates and lentil plant protein makes it a balanced source of energy and nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The rice‑lentil combination is traditional in Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cuisines.
Lentils are rich in iron, while rice provides a quick source of glucose.
The dish stores well and reheats quickly, making it popular in cafeterias and on‑the‑go meals.
A low‑salt version is suitable for sodium‑restricted diets.

items.title: Balanced source of protein and carbs
items.content: Lentils supply plant protein and rice delivers easily digestible carbohydrates, supporting sustained energy.

items.title: Rich in iron and folate
items.content: Lentils contain iron and folic acid, important for blood formation and nervous‑system health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The product contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Lentils add fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Supports blood‑sugar control
items.content: The mix of slowly digestible lentil carbs and faster rice carbs helps moderate the glycemic response.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to lentils.

items.title: Presence of antinutrients
items.content: Lentils contain phytic acid, which in large amounts can reduce mineral absorption.

items.title: High glycemic index of white rice
items.content: White rice can raise blood glucose quickly; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product can be eaten on its own, added to salads, soups, or used as a side dish for meat and fish. Feel free to season with herbs, spices, or a drizzle of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep refrigerated, where it stays fresh for up to 7 days.
